text:
alex: Bringing up raptor-3b-ptq on the int8 pool — observed a bunch of funcall responses where the tool args are double-escaped strings. Looks like nested JSON is being serialized as a string literal. Example below.

tara: Can you paste a raw output snippet?

alex: ```
{"role":"tool","name":"email_sender","content":"{\"recipient\":\"test@example.com\",\"subject\":\"Hi\",\"body\":\"Hello\nThanks\"}"}
```

jit: Yep that's double-escaped nested JSON: the tool content itself is a JSON string containing JSON. Two quick suspects: streaming escape layer + model output including literal backslashes, or tokenizer quirks from PTQ introducing extra escape tokens.

sasha: We've seen similar in the int8 canary a while back — PTQ tokenization shifts can insert backslashes or split escape sequences across tokens. It shows up more with nested JSON and long string fields.

chloe: Proposal: run a focused eval (2k samples) comparing parse-success and rescue heuristics. Heuristics to test: 1) double-unescape (parse-string-then-parse), 2) ndjson-split (split on line breaks, parse each line), 3) json5/lenient parse. Measure parse-success, schema-acceptance, and downstream-tool-errors.

chloe: Example eval command:```
python tools/eval_toolcalls.py --model raptor-3b-ptq --n 2000 --heuristics double_unescape,ndjson,json5 --out /tmp/raptor_toolcall_eval.json
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started on eng-ml-ptqpool-2 (pool id: ptq-2).

alex: Ran a quick 200 sample run: baseline parse success = 0.83, double-unescape rescue bumps to 0.97 but produces ~1.5% incorrect arg shapes (e.g., args parsed but missing required keys) that caused tool runtime errors. Without schema check the rescue looks great, but it silently masks malformed payloads.

tara: So we need to gate rescue with schema verification. If rescue produces parsed JSON but fails schema, treat as parse failure (allow retry/rescue fallback). Also consider restricting rescue to small responses (<512 tokens) or when the function name is present.

jit: Also watch retry budget — we shouldn't add heavy retries for every request. Instead: attempt single-parse -> if fails, attempt cheap rescue (double-unescape) locally and validate schema -> if both fail and client retry budget allows, run 1 retry with lower temperature and logging. Correlate with trace id to avoid double-counting.

sasha: Add telemetry fields: toolcall.parse.v1, toolcall.rescue.method, toolcall.rescue.result, token_prefix_id, kvcache_prefix_hash. Store raw tokens + detokenized output for failing items for offline analysis.

chloe: I'll run the 2k eval with those telemetry flags and produce a small dashboard with parse success, schema pass, downstream error rate, and rescue false-positive rate. Will also include token-length buckets.

alex: Cool — if rescue false-positives are concentrated in a small class (nested stringified objects with >3 levels), maybe we should add a schema-aware rescue that only attempts double-unescape for fields annotated as "stringified_json" in the tool contract.

tara: Good idea. Also add a canary rollout gate: enable rescue for 10% of traffic with heavy telemetry for two days before making it default.

chloe: I'll kick off the eval now and post results in this thread. Need thumbs if anyone objects to telemetry keys or the 10% canary plan.

alex: No objections from me. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: ticket created: ML-PTQ-ESC-112 (investigate PTQ escape sequences)

chloe: tagging @sasha @jit for the eval run, will ping when data is in grafana.

alex: Thanks — follow-up expected with numbers and concrete next steps.
